title: session-spark-notebook
body:
Quick context / top-level idea:

A lightweight, user-configurable session template feature that lets apps save small, opinionated "session presets" (persona + system priming + canned context selectors) to speed frequent conversational workflows. Target: 1) reduce token waste for repeat flows; 2) make common tasks 2–3x faster to start; 3) provide a simple UX for product teams to expose curated prompts without shipping backend changes.

Why this now:
- Customers are asking for easier ways to provide consistent assistant behavior across product flows (support macros, onboarding flows, forms).
- We already have session-level KV caching and snapshot APIs — a surface to build on.
- Small win for PLG adoption: shareable preset links could be viral inside orgs.

Problem statement (working):
Users of apps backed by Redwood-powered assistants repeatedly craft the same prompt/priming and manually re-send context (few-shot examples, domain hints). This causes: inconsistent outputs, higher token spend, and friction onboarding new users or replicating workflows across teammates.

Goals (must-have vs nice-to-have):
- Must-have: minimal API/SDK surface (create/get/list/apply template), client-side UX pattern and stored preset object that maps to a small set of model-serving knobs (system prompt, instruction slot, preloaded embeddings, context slice selectors).
- Must-have: ability to attach a preset to a route + optional autosave of short-term session variables (e.g., user name, account id) mapped to placeholders.
- Nice-to-have: share links, team-libraries, per-preset quality grades (from micro-evals).
- Nice-to-have: UI in Console to create and preview templates (WYSIWYG with live sample responses).

Success metrics (initial):
- Adoption: X% of new chat sessions start with a preset within 30 days for customers that enable feature (set target 15%).
- Token delta: average token-per-session reduces by 18% for users using presets vs baseline after 2 weeks.
- Time-to-first-meaningful-reply (TTFMR) reduced by 30% for preset-backed flows.
- Qualitative: CS feedback — fewer support threads about prompt inconsistency.

Proposed object model (sketch):
- preset_id (string)
- title (string)
- description (string)
- author (user id)
- system_prompt (short text)
- instruction_template (text with placeholders: {{customer_name}})
- context_selectors (list of selectors: "last_n_messages", "kb:faq", "saved_snippet:welcome_flow")
- default_model_hint (optional)
- qos_profile (e.g., low-latency, cost-optimized)
- visibility: personal|team|org

UI/UX notes (for quick sketch):
- In-app composer: small dropdown labelled "Start from preset" with thumbnails + one-click apply.
- Preset editor: two-column: left = template fields, right = live sample with toggles for model/hint/fidelity.
- Placeholder editor: map placeholders to session vars or ask-on-launch prompts.
- Lite console view: list + usage counts + last-used by.

User stories (draft examples):
1) As a customer support agent, I want a "triage" preset that preloads recent order history and a short system tone so I can answer refund questions consistently without re-priming each time.
2) As a product manager, I want a shared preset for our onboarding flow so new hires get identical assistant behavior when they test flows.
3) As a developer, I want an API to programmatically apply a preset to an outbound request so I can A/B different presets without changing my code.

Edge cases / constraints:
- Sensitive placeholders (account id, PII) must be redacted in presets and use runtime substitution only; ensure no accidental storage in shared presets.
- Preset size: cap system+instruction at ~4k tokens to avoid performance surprises.
- Conflicting selectors: if preset requests a context slice not available in route, fallback policy should be explicit (ignore selector vs. prompt user).

Instrumentation / telemetry:
- Track preset_apply_count, preset_create_count, avg_tokens_before_after, sample_responses for drift analysis.
- Add rollout flag: >2 weeks telemetry before allowing share links default on orgs.

Rollout & experiments:
- Phase 0 (internal): implement API + CLI tool + internal presets for SRE/CS to dogfood (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (beta opt-in): expose in Console for a small % of orgs; collect metrics and micro-evals (4 weeks).
- Experiment: default faint-presets for new accounts vs. no-presets -> measure onboarding completion.

Open questions (TODO):
- Storage: should presets live in control plane (central) or be namespaced per-tenant DB? (pros/cons: sharing vs. cross-org leakage)
- Visibility model: granular ACLs needed? invite-only team libraries? cost of adding ACL layer vs. quick wins.
- How to handle model-specific content (e.g., quantized vs full fp) when a preset pins a model hint and that model isn't available in Dedicated/private deployments? Need fallback mapping.
- UI: Do we auto-suggest presets from high-frequency conversation clusters? (Privacy implications)

Dependencies / owners (initial):
- API & SDK: Miles (owner) + Eng (2w prototype)
- Console preview UI: Lena (owner) + Design rapid mockups
- Security/Compliance: must sign off redaction/placeholder logic (Evan)

Quick technical sketch for apply flow:
Client -> POST /v1/sessions.start {preset_id, placeholder_values, model_hint}
Control plane resolves preset -> composes final system + instruction -> resolves context_selectors by querying session store / KB -> sends to serving runtime with qos_profile.

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: presets become a vector to leak protected context (mitigate: strict redaction + opt-in sharing defaults to personal).
- Risk: UX complexity if too many presets (mitigate: favorites, search, tagging).

Next immediate steps (my personal TODOs):
- Build minimal API proto (create/get/list/apply) + example curl snippets.
- Mock Console editor in Figma (2 simple screens) and get PM/design sync.
- Draft security requirements for placeholder handling and ask Evan for a short review.
- Schedule 30-min sync with Miles to scope prototype timeline.

Notes to self (raw):
- consider quick win: "invoice-responder" preset with canned error-handling heuristics (could be 1-week internal dogfood).
- keep preset schema tiny at first; add fancy team-libraries later.
- think about micro-eval hook: run a small set of golden prompts whenever preset changes to detect regressions.

Random brainstorm ideas to maybe add later:
- marketplace of community presets (curated) with ratings
- one-click export of preset -> SDK snippet to embed in product code
- preset versioning with diffs and rollbacks

End of pad. This is rough — will refine after initial dev sync.
